accept: pulmonary hypertension with right heart failure

findings: Right axis deviation with right ventricular hypertrophy
Tall R in lead V1 with deep S in lead V6

echoTasks.find: D shaped left ventricle with septal flattening in systole and diastole
Dense triangular tricuspid jet with a raised right atrial pressure estimate
Dilated inferior vena cava with minimal collapse on sniff

auscultation.added: Right sided fourth sound with a palpable right ventricular heave
auscultation.murmur: Pansystolic murmur of functional tricuspid regurgitation

exam.general: Young woman, breathless on minimal exertion, dusky lips, raised venous pressure to the jaw
exam.jvp: Markedly raised with prominent v waves
exam.other: Tender liver 3 cm, ascites with shifting dullness, ankle oedema

history.a: Two years of progressive breathlessness, now NYHA class IV, one syncope last month
No wheeze, dry cough only, no haemoptysis
No clot history, no appetite suppressants, no HIV risk disclosed
On diuretics with partial relief, no targeted therapy
Tailor, stopped work 6 months ago, anxious about prognosis
Mother has high blood pressure, no lung disease in the family

keyPoints: Refer urgently to a pulmonary hypertension centre for right heart catheterisation and vasoreactivity testing
Complete cause seeking workup including CT angiography, lung function, sleep study and connective tissue screen
Start diuretics for congestion and oxygen where hypoxic while avoiding unproven vasodilators
Risk stratify with walk distance, natriuretic peptides and right ventricular function for therapy escalation
Counsel on pregnancy avoidance, anaesthesia risk and supervised rehabilitation
management.model: Urgent referral with full cause seeking workup, congestion control, formal risk stratification, and life planning counsel

sources: ESC guideline on pulmonary hypertension, in own words
ASE guidance on echocardiographic assessment of pulmonary hypertension, in own words
stem: A 39 year old tailor from Kanpur reports two years of progressive breathlessness with a recent syncope. Lips are dusky, the second heart sound is loud with a parasternal heave, and the ECG shows right ventricular hypertrophy.
teaching: High means velocity above 3.4 m per s with pressure above 50 mmHg
Septal flattening in both systole and diastole marks combined pressure and volume overload
Syncope in pulmonary hypertension is a red flag for low output and needs urgent referral
Fellow quantification adds TAPSE, atrial size and risk scores to the pressure estimate
title: High probability pulmonary hypertension with right heart failure
